## What does this table tell us? {#l2-opening-table}

A survey records the number of pets in **50 households**.

| Number of pets, $x$ | Frequency, $f$ |
|:---:|:---:|
| 0 | 15 |
| 1 | 20 |
| 2 | 10 |
| 3 | 4 |
| 4 | 1 |

::: {.takeaway}
What does the 20 represent? How many households have **at most one pet**?
:::
<p class="booklet-cue">Example 3.4 dataset · Booklet p. 39</p>

::: notes
After the title slide, begin the teaching with the familiar two-column frequency table. Students have met frequency tables and histograms in Years 9–10. The 20 is the number of households with exactly one pet. At most one includes zero and one: 15+20=35. Collect reasoning without adding columns yet; this motivates cumulative frequency. Keep the distinction between number of pets and number of households explicit.
:::
